title: Demand Signal Fusion and Burst Resilience Manual
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Summary

This document defines a practical approach for fusing heterogeneous demand signals (telemetry, request semantics, tenant profiles) to make deterministic, explainable decisions during traffic bursts. It pairs decision heuristics with concrete alert rules, scaling actions, and integration examples for our operational tooling (Prometheus, Alertmanager, Capacity Orchestrator). The goal is to preserve customer-facing SLOs while minimizing cost and churn during transient and sustained traffic events.

Scope

- Audience: SREs, oncall, runtime engineers, product owners for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Systems covered: inference-gateway, batching-service, model-warm-pool, admission-controller, capacity-orchestrator.
- Not covered: billing reconciliation, legal/customer communications (see customer-success).

Definitions

- Demand signal: any metric or event that correlates with upcoming or current request load (examples below).
- Burst: a >3x baseline increase in RPS or token-rate sustained for >30s and <30m.
- Surge: burst that continues >30m.
- Headroom: available capacity reservable for latency-sensitive tenants without violating SLOs.

Key telemetry & signals to fuse

1) Ingress signals (real-time):
   - rps_total, rps_per_route, token_rate
   - queue_depth (per route / per pod)
   - request_duration_p50/p95/p99

2) Backend resource signals:
   - gpu_utilization, gpu_memory_pressure, host_load_1m
   - model_kv_cache_hit_rate, model_warm_pool_free_slots

3) System events & semantic signals:
   - model_variant_fallbacks (counts)
   - tenant_priority_header (high/standard/low)
   - large-batch-job-submitted (boolean/event)

4) External signals (optional):
   - scheduled-marketing-campaigns (calendar feed)
   - infra-degradation (cloud provider health API)

Fusion heuristics (high level)

- Short-window aggregation: compute 15s rolling window aggregates for RPS/token_rate and 60s for queue_depth and GPU metrics.
- Priority-weighting: multiply tenant-specified priority weight (2.0 high, 1.0 standard, 0.5 low) when calculating effective demand.
- Signal consensus: escalate to SRE action if >=2 independent signals cross thresholds (ingress + backend or ingress + model_kv cache drop).
- Burst classification:
  - transient: burst duration < 30s — prefer local admission and soft-throttling.
  - sustained-burst: 30s–30m — prefer warm-pool expansion and non-disruptive routing.
  - surge: >30m — engage reserved capacity and formal capacity reallocation.

Decision matrix (example)

| Observed condition (consensus) | Immediate action (automated) | Escalation threshold | Oncall action | Rationale |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 3x RPS spike, queue_depth < 50, GPU utilization < 60% | Increase concurrent batch window by +20% on low-prio routes | N/A | Monitor | Use batching to accept transient increase without new capacity |
| 5x RPS, queue_depth > 200, kv_cache_hit_rate < 70% | Trigger warm-pool: +2 warm GPUs; mark low-prio tenants degraded | 90s sustained | Page SRE | Warm pool reduces cold starts and stabilizes latency |
| Backend GPU mem pressure > 85% and p99 latency rising | Evict background batch jobs; enable shed-on-low-priority=true | immediate | Page SRE | Maintain SLOs for high-priority tenants |
| Surge > 30m with sustained error budget burn > 5% | Activate reserved capacity swap (capacity-orchestrator) | sustained 30m | Page + Alert customer-facing comms owner | Ensure durable capacity; coordinate with sales/CS |

Concrete thresholds (recommended starting point)

- rps spike factor: 3.0 (burst), 5.0 (critical)
- queue_depth critical: 200 requests total across cluster
- kv_cache_hit_rate warning: < 80% ; critical: < 70%
- gpu_utilization critical: > 90% for >120s
- model_warm_pool_free_slots low: < 10% of pool size

Prometheus alert examples

1) Burst-detection rule (15s window):

ALERT BurstDetected
IF increase(requests_total[15s]) / avg(requests_total[5m]) > 3
FOR 15s
LABELS { severity = "warning", category = "demand" }
ANNOTATIONS { summary = "Detected 15s RPS spike >3x baseline" }

2) KV cache degradation alert:

ALERT KVCacheDegradation
IF avg_over_time(model_kv_cache_hit_rate[1m]) < 0.75
FOR 30s
LABELS { severity = "critical", category = "model" }
ANNOTATIONS { summary = "KV cache hit rate below 75%" }

Operational tooling integrations

- Capacity Orchestrator (CO): define policies for warm-pool expansion, reserved-capacity swaps, and preemptible eviction. Example policy snippet YAML (CO):

policy_name: burst-warmup
min_warm_gpus: 2
max_warm_gpus: 8
scale_step: 2
scale_cooldown: 90 # seconds
triggers:
  - metric: kv_cache_hit_rate
    operator: lt
    value: 0.75
    window: 60s
  - metric: queue_depth
    operator: gt
    value: 150
    window: 30s

- Admission Controller: add a soft throttle knob that reduces allowed concurrency for low-priority tenants by a configurable fraction. Example CLI to simulate:

# reduce low-priority concurrency by 50%
./admctl set-tenant-guardrail --tenant-group low --concurrency-factor 0.5 --reason "burst response"

Runbook: immediate triage for an ongoing burst (15–90s window)

1) Verify the signals: check the four categories above and confirm consensus (at least two). Quick checklist:
   - Grafana dashboard: rps_total, queue_depth, p99 latency, gpu_utilization, kv_cache_hit_rate.
   - Prometheus alerts firing: BurstDetected OR KVCacheDegradation.
2) Apply non-disruptive mitigations (automated preferred):
   - Increase batching concurrency on low-priority routes (automated via API)
   - Trigger warm-pool expansion by policy: CO API -> apply policy "burst-warmup"
3) If latency still rising after scale_step with 60s cooldown, escalate to SRE (page) and mark affected tenants with degraded_status=true in topology db.
2) Document actions in incident tracker ticket and tag: demand-fusion-burst.

Runbook: sustained surge (30m+)

1) Confirm sustained signals and error budget burn. Calculate projected error budget depletion using current burn rate.
2) Initiate reserved capacity swap: call CO runbook: swap reserved for inference-gateway.
3) Coordinate with Product & CS for messaging if any high-priority customers may be impacted.
4) Kick off an incident review with a hypothesis: root cause = demand mismatch vs provisioning; include signal fusion artifact.

Post-incident review checklist (required for any burst that caused SLO degradation):

- Attach the fused-signal log (see logging spec below) to the postmortem.
- Validate that decision matrix mapping matched observed outcome or document deviations.
- Update thresholds if false positives/negatives contributed to delay.
- Schedule a 2-week follow-up to run a controlled surge replay in staging.

Fused-signal logging spec (single-line JSON per event)

- Fields (flat key set): timestamp, window_start, window_end, rps_total, rps_factor_vs_baseline, queue_depth, gpu_util, kv_cache_hit_rate, warm_pool_free_slots, consensus_signals, action_taken, action_origin, action_id

Example (single-line JSON stored in log-index):
{ "timestamp":"2026-12-03T14:12:05Z", "window_start":"2026-12-03T14:11:50Z", "window_end":"2026-12-03T14:12:05Z", "rps_total":"4200", "rps_factor_vs_baseline":"3.6", "queue_depth":"240", "gpu_util":"88", "kv_cache_hit_rate":"0.68", "warm_pool_free_slots":"1", "consensus_signals":"[ingress,model]", "action_taken":"warm-pool-scale+2,evict-background-jobs", "action_origin":"automated-policy:burst-warmup", "action_id":"co-20261203-001" }

Tooling validation & test harnesses

- Synthetic replay: use the burst-replay tool to re-ingest recorded ingress traces with modulated RPS and tenant-priority weights. Command example:

burst-replay --trace-id 2026-11-30-bigtth --rps-multiplier 4 --tenant-weight high:1.5,low:0.5 --duration 5m

- Canary test: before applying new thresholds in production, run a canary in a shadow cluster that mirrors 2% of traffic and verify fused-signal decisions for at least 3 synthetic bursts.

Ownership & SLA alignment

- Owners: SRE runtime (primary), Serving Runtime (secondary), Capacity Orchestrator team (policy maintenance).
- SLO implications: ensure that actions preserve p99 latency SLO for high-priority tenants 99.95% monthly. If preserved only via degradation of low-priority tenants, record that as controlled remediation.

Change control & rollout guidance

- All threshold changes require: unit tests in alerting harness, a canary run (2% traffic mirror) for 72 hours, and a post-canonical runbook review with SRE lead.
- Emergency tweak path: oncall SRE can bypass canary if >5% error budget at 24h projection; document the reason in the incident ticket.

Appendix: quick reference commands

- Force warm pool expansion (CO):
  curl -XPOST https://co.internal/api/v1/policies/burst-warmup/trigger -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CO_TOKEN'

- Evict background batch jobs:
  ./batchctl evict --label background=true --max-evict 5

- Read fused-signal logs for time range:
  es-query "index=fused-signals AND @timestamp:[2026-12-03T14:00 TO 2026-12-03T15:00]"
